Seven numbers, six multiplications

Α–Η label the proof’s numbers. They form a progression, each 9:8 of its predecessor. We realize their ratios as increasing frequencies. They are not labeled as string lengths. Frequencies and cents below are rounded modern calculations.

531441 > 2 × 262144 = 524288. The excess is 7153. Dividing by the octave gives 531441/524288, or 23.460010 cents, commonly called the Pythagorean comma.

Six modern 200-cent steps close the octave by changing each step to 2^(1/6), approximately 1.122462. The source's 9/8 is 1.125. Modern algebra also gives the same comma from twelve 3:2 fifths compared with seven octaves: (3/2)^12 ÷ 2^7 = 531441/524288. This connection is an explanation added here, not a quotation from IX.

Read proposition XIV

The work is transmitted under Euclid's name; authorship is not settled here. Greek text and Latin translation: Heinrich Menge, Euclidis opera omnia VIII (Leipzig, 1916), pp. 174–175. English translations and notes are new. The selected app sentence was 3; every sentence is included below.

The claim · XIV

Τὸ διὰ πασῶν ἔλαττον ἢ ἓξ τόνων.

diapason minus est quam sex tonorum.

The octave is smaller than six tones.

ἔλαττον / minus means ‘smaller’; ἢ / quam introduces the comparison. ‘Tone’ here has the 9:8 ratio established in XIII. A modern 200-cent whole tone changes that premise.

The musical premises · XII and XIII

δέδεικται γὰρ τὸ μὲν διὰ πασῶν διπλάσιον, ὁ δὲ τόνος ἐπόγδοος·

nam demonstratum est, diapason duplum esse [prop. XII], tonum vero sesqueoctavum [prop. XIII].

For it has been shown that the octave is double, while the tone is a whole and an eighth.

δέδεικται / demonstratum est points back to earlier proofs. διπλάσιον / duplum names 2:1; ἐπόγδοος / sesqueoctavum names 9:8. Menge adds the proposition references in square brackets to the Latin.

The numerical premise · IX

τὰ δὲ ἓξ ἐπόγδοα διαστήματα μείζονα διαστήματός [ἐστι] διπλασίου.

verum sex intervalla sesqueoctava intervallo duplo sunt maiora [prop. IX].

But six intervals of a whole and an eighth are greater than a double interval.

μείζονα / maiora means ‘greater’. The seven source integers supply six successive ratios, each 9:8. The Greek bracketed [ἐστι] is retained from this edition; it is not silently promoted to certain text.

The conclusion · XIV

τὸ ἄρα διὰ πασῶν ἔλαττόν ἐστιν ἓξ τόνων.

ergo diapason minus est sex tonis.

Therefore the octave is smaller than six tones.

ἄρα / ergo carries the inference. Greek ἓξ τόνων and Latin sex tonis express the comparison. The numerical contradiction belongs to these ratios; it does not make modern equal temperament impossible.

Four words in the argument

διὰ πασῶν · dia pasōn · diapason · octave
Literally ‘through all’. Here it names the consonance with ratio 2:1. The phrase is quoted in its printed form, not translated as ‘all notes’ in the proof.
τόνος · tonos · tonus · tone
The tone in XIII is the interval left when a 4:3 fourth is removed from a 3:2 fifth: (3/2) ÷ (4/3) = 9/8. Removing a musical interval divides ratios; it does not subtract their numerical values.
ἐπόγδοος · epogdoos · sesqueoctavus · a whole and an eighth
A quantity contains the other plus one eighth of it: 1 + 1/8 = 9/8. Each selected source row after Α adds one eighth of the preceding integer.
διπλάσιον · diplasion · duplum · double
An octave doubles frequency in this modern realization. At step six the source's target is twice 262144, or 524288. Compare that with Η = 531441.
